name: mlx-serve
tagline: A native Zig inference server for Apple Silicon — no Python
description: mlx-serve is a native inference server for Apple Silicon written in Zig, built on MLX and GGUF. It exposes OpenAI-, Anthropic-, and Ollama-compatible APIs with no Python in the stack, and measures roughly 26% faster decode than LM Studio. Speculative decoding, continuous batching, and KV-cache quantization squeeze more throughput out of unified memory, and the MLX Core app layers chat, agent mode, MCP tools, and image, video, music, speech, and 3D generation on top. A single static binary makes LAN model sharing between Macs trivial, and it can run DeepSeek V4 Flash.
highlights: Native Zig inference server on MLX + GGUF with no Python in the stack
Speculative decoding, continuous batching, and KV-cache quantization
MLX Core app with chat, agent mode, MCP tools, and multimodal generation
curatorNote: A single Zig binary serving OpenAI-compatible endpoints from Apple Silicon, no Python anywhere, and measurably faster than LM Studio. The trend of ditching Python for native inference servers just got a very strong entry.
